source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I’d like us to change direction: please reset the design around our original Hero V, which I still consider the strongest version, and stop scaling the second V mathematically. From that anchor, explore an optically drawn second V instead. It should share the alphabet’s design language and DNA while naturally serving as a supporting form. Keep the extended right arm as the signature detail, matching it optically to the Hero V, but achieve that result through drawing rather than pure scaling.

Looking back through the earlier proofs and these explorations clarified the problem. Although the reduction is technically proportional, the resulting V appears to belong to a different alphabet; mathematical reduction causes it to lose some of the character and presence that make the Hero V so compelling.

I’m attaching my current favorite image as the preferred reference, though it lacks the desired right-arm extension. Taking this optical approach should produce a more cohesive, timeless wordmark in which every letter feels deliberately crafted instead of mechanically derived.

value_updates.signature_sweep_usage: The expressive Hero V right-arm gesture remains excluded from the E and L forms; the optically drawn second V is outside that exclusion and uses an extended right arm matched optically to the Hero V.
value_updates.fixed_asset_boundary: Explore and refine the remaining letterforms around the original Hero V and unchanged É accent; the second V is reopened for optical drawing under the client's explicit change request.

decisions.reason: The source necessarily extends the signature right-arm language back to the second V, but through optical matching rather than literal shared geometry.
